children: Banks listed on the Muscat Stock Exchange (MSX) recorded a combined net profit of RO455mn in the first nine months of 2026, an increase of 8.2% from RO420.6mn in the same period last year, as most Omani lenders reported higher earnings.
The seven listed banks also recorded growth in their combined assets and shareholders’ equity, reflecting an expansion in the sector’s balance sheet during the period.

According to an Oman News Agency report, the banking sector’s performance was supported by increased financing for development and private sector projects, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and personal loans. Improved risk management, lower provisions at some banks and continued investment in digital banking services were also cited as factors supporting earnings.
Bank Muscat remained the largest profit contributor, reporting net profit of RO209.1mn, up 9.2% from RO191.5mn in the first nine months of 2025.
Sohar International Bank ranked second, with net profit rising to RO77.6mn from RO70.7mn, while National Bank of Oman (NBO) recorded a profit of RO57.5mn, compared with RO51.7mn a year earlier.
BankDhofar’s net profit increased to RO38.8mn from RO36mn, while Ahlibank reported a 12.5% increase to RO36.5mn from RO32.4mn. Oman Arab Bank’s consolidated net profit rose to RO28.1mn from RO23.3mn.

Bank Nizwa was the only lender among the seven to report a decline in net profit this year. Its earnings fell 52% to RO7mn from RO14.8mn in the corresponding period last year. The decline came as the bank’s provisions more than doubled to RO13.6mn from approximately RO6.2mn. Operating expenses increased to RO23.8mn from RO20.8mn, while operating profit fell to RO21.5mn from RO23.3mn.
The consolidated financial statements of the seven banks showed that their combined assets reached approximately RO50.2bn at the end of September 2026, up 13.7% from RO44.1bn a year earlier.

Bank Muscat had the largest asset base, at approximately RO16bn, followed by Sohar International Bank with RO10.2bn. BankDhofar ranked third with RO6.3bn, while NBO’s assets stood at approximately RO6.1bn.

Combined shareholders’ equity of Omani banks increased 9.8% to more than RO7bn at the end of September 2026, compared with RO6.3bn in September 2025. The increase was attributed to higher profits, reserves and capital.
Bank Muscat led in shareholders’ equity with RO2.7bn, followed by Sohar International with RO1.1bn, NBO with RO928mn and Oman Arab Bank with RO709.6mn.
The banks also pursued capital-strengthening measures and strategic initiatives during the first nine months of the year.
Bank Muscat’s extraordinary general meeting approved an increase in its authorised capital from RO800mn to RO1.2bn.
Sohar International, meanwhile, offered more than one billion shares through the exercise of pre-emptive rights, with the move set to increase its capital from RO702.5mn to approximately RO850mn.
The measures formed part of broader efforts by the listed lenders to strengthen their capital bases, improve asset quality and pursue domestic and international expansion.

title: ZAWYA: Omani banks’ 9-month total profits rise 8.2%
